prediction.text:
Disney attributed the Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) operating income improvement in fiscal 2024 to "improved results at Disney+". Operating income was $143 million, against an operating loss of $2,496 million a year earlier. The MD&A gives no separate quantified bridge. It does show subscription fee and advertising revenue growth. It also shows lower non-sports content costs at Disney+.
Disney reported that DTC operating results increased $2,639 million, to operating income of $143 million from an operating loss of $2,496 million, "due to improved results at Disney+." The MD&A does not give a separate quantified bridge for the change.
On the cost side, Disney said the decrease in programming and production costs at Disney+ and other was attributable to lower costs for non-sports content available on Disney+. This was partially offset by higher costs for cricket programming at Disney+ Hotstar.
On the revenue side, Disney said subscription fee growth reflected a 10% increase from higher effective rates due to retail pricing increases and 6% from subscriber growth, partially offset by a 2% decrease from an unfavorable Foreign Exchange Impact.
Disney said higher advertising revenue reflected a 26% increase from higher impressions, partially offset by a 12% decrease from lower rates.

caveats: Management attributes the swing only to "improved results at Disney+". The revenue and cost drivers above are the supporting explanations in the MD&A, not a quantified attribution of the operating income change.
The DTC operating expense table chunk was not fully reviewed, so coverage of the cost drivers may be incomplete.
